steps.body: An expression must name exactly one value, so the order of operations is a convention that settles ties: multiplication and division act before addition and subtraction.
steps.narration: An expression must name exactly one value, so the order of operations is a convention that settles ties: multiplication and division act before addition and subtraction.

widget.prompt: Build 6 × 7 as six equal bars of 7, before anything is subtracted.
widget.successFeedback: 42 — the product forms first, and only then does a subtraction act on it.
widget.partialFeedback: Every group holds the same 7; build each bar to 7.

predict.reveal: Working left to right would give 35, but multiplication binds first, so 4 × 5 = 20 and 3 joins it.

cml.actionGoal: Resolve the groupings, then the ranks, and watch the value the expression names settle for g5e order.
invariants: An expression names ONE value, and the order conventions plus any grouping symbols are what guarantee it: change the grouping and you change the quantity, which is why g5e order is about structure rather than arithmetic.
misconceptions: Working strictly left to right across different ranks, dropping a grouping when reading an expression aloud, or describing a multiplicative pattern with a constant difference.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the brackets moved one term to the left, what value would the expression name instead?

options.label: Because you always work left to right
options.feedback: Left to right would give 35. It applies only among operations of equal rank, not across ranks.

options.label: Because 3 is the smallest number
options.feedback: Size never decides order; the operation's rank does.

options.label: Both answers are acceptable
options.feedback: Only one is: the convention exists precisely so that an expression names a single value.
